name: Electric lawn mower (corded)
note: Usually 12-13 A. Needs a heavy outdoor cord; 100 ft is a stretch.

name: Leaf blower (corded)
note: Usually 12 A. Use a 12 gauge outdoor cord for 50 ft or more.

name: String trimmer (corded)
note: About 5 A. A 16 gauge outdoor cord is fine up to about 100 ft.

name: Hedge trimmer (corded)
note: About 4 A. Keep the cord behind you and away from the blade.

name: Chainsaw (corded)
note: 14-15 A: at the limit of a household outlet. Short, thick cord only.

name: Pressure washer (electric)
note: 13-15 A. Many manuals say use a longer hose instead of a longer cord. Always on a GFCI.

name: Wood chipper / leaf mulcher (electric)
note: About 15 A with a hard start. Plug in close to the outlet.

name: Garden tiller / cultivator (electric)
note: About 10 A.

name: Bug zapper
note: Small load; usually runs all night.

name: Snow blower (corded electric)
note: 13-15 A. Use the thickest, shortest outdoor cord you can; cold makes cords stiff.

name: Snow shovel (electric, corded)
note: About 10 A.

name: Snow blower electric start button
note: Only for the few seconds it cranks the engine, but it pulls hard. Unplug once running.

name: Engine block heater
note: Usually 400-1000 W; check the cord tag. Runs for hours, so use a 14 gauge or thicker outdoor cord. A timer saves power.

name: Roof / gutter de-icing cable (100 ft)
note: About 5 W per foot. Must be on a GFCI.

name: Pipe heat cable (about 30 ft)
note: Roughly 3-8 W per foot depending on the brand.

name: Heated driveway mat
note: Varies a lot by size; check the label.

name: LED Christmas lights (100-bulb string)
note: Check the tag for how many strings can be connected end to end (often 20-40+).

name: Incandescent mini lights (100-bulb string)
note: Old-style strings: usually only 3 can be connected end to end.

name: LED C9 lights (25-bulb string)
note: Check the tag for the end-to-end limit.

name: Incandescent C9 lights (25-bulb string)
note: Big old-style bulbs. 4 strings already need a 14 gauge cord at 100 ft.

name: Inflatable yard decoration
note: A fan plus lights: usually 50-150 W.

name: Holiday light projector
note: Very small load.

name: LED flood light
note: Replaces a 250-500 W halogen.

name: Halogen work light
note: Gets very hot. Keep away from anything that can burn.

name: LED work light
note: Much cooler and lighter load than halogen.

name: Heated pet bed
note: Small ones use 4-6 W; outdoor pads up to about 40-60 W.

name: Heated pet water bowl
note: Usually 25-100 W.

name: Heated bird bath
note: Usually 75-200 W.

name: Heated poultry waterer
note: Runs all winter. Keep the plug connection off the ground and dry.

name: Stock tank heater
note: Uses as much as a space heater, around the clock. 12 gauge outdoor cord and its own GFCI outlet.

name: Heat lamp (250 W bulb)
note: A common barn fire cause. Clamp it securely, with a guard, away from bedding.

name: Brooder heat plate
note: Safer than a heat lamp for chicks.

name: Electric fence charger (plug-in)
note: Tiny load; usually 2-10 W.

name: Shop vac
note: Label usually says 12-13 A. Short bursts, but a big starting pull.

name: Circular saw
note: Usually 15 A. 12 gauge cord, as short as possible.

name: Miter saw
note: Usually 15 A.

name: Table saw (job site)
note: Usually 15 A. Don't run another big tool on the same circuit.

name: Reciprocating saw
note: Usually 10-12 A.

name: Angle grinder
note: Usually 7-11 A.

name: Drill (corded)
note: Usually 5-8 A.

name: Bench grinder
note: Usually 2-4 A.

name: Air compressor (pancake, 6 gal)
note: Starts hard every time it cycles. Manuals usually say add air hose instead of extension cord.

name: Tire inflator (120 V)
note: Small plug-in inflators; check the label.

name: Heat gun
note: Usually 12-13 A.

name: Flux-core welder (120 V)
note: Usually needs a 20 A outlet. Too much for a household extension cord; see the manual for the cord size it allows.

name: Garage ceiling fan / box fan
note: Usually 50-120 W.

name: Space heater
note: Pulls the most of anything in the house. Give it its own wall outlet.

name: Oil-filled radiator heater
note: Same load as any space heater: wall outlet only.

name: Patio heater (electric)
note: 12.5 A for hours. Outdoor 12 gauge cord, kept short, on a GFCI.

name: Window air conditioner (small)
note: 5,000-6,000 BTU units. Plug straight into the wall.

name: Portable air conditioner
note: Plug straight into the wall.

name: Dehumidifier
note: Most manuals say no extension cords.

name: Electric blanket
note: Usually 50-200 W.

name: Sump pump (1/3 HP)
note: Plug straight into a GFCI wall outlet.

name: Utility / transfer pump
note: For draining. Keep the plug end high and dry.

name: Fountain / pond pump (small)
note: Usually 20-100 W. GFCI outlet.

name: Pond de-icer
note: Usually 250-1500 W around the clock. GFCI outlet.

name: Electric smoker
note: Runs for hours. 14 gauge outdoor cord, kept short.

name: Pellet grill
note: About 300 W while the igniter heats, then about 50 W.

name: Electric griddle / hot plate
note: Don't share the circuit with other cooking.

name: Slow cooker
note: Usually 150-300 W.

name: Coffee maker
note: Usually 600-1200 W.

name: Microwave
note: A "1000 W" microwave pulls about 1500 W from the wall. Plug straight in.

name: Electric kettle
note: Short use, but at the limit with anything else on.

name: Mini fridge
note: Fridge makers say no extension cords. Starting pull is several times the running watts.

name: Chest freezer
note: Fridge makers say no extension cords.

name: Battery maintainer (trickle charger)
note: About 0.75-1.5 A on the battery side, but only about 0.2-0.4 A from the wall. Bigger 10 A chargers pull much more.

name: Battery charger (10 A)
note: Check the input amps on the label (often 1.5-2 A). Engine-start chargers pull much more while starting.

name: Power tool battery charger
note: Usually 50-150 W.

name: E-bike charger
note: Usually 100-250 W for several hours.

name: Electric car charger (Level 1)
note: 12 A for 10+ hours. Car makers say plug straight into a dedicated wall outlet, no extension cord.

name: Laptop charger
note: Usually 45-100 W.

name: Phone charger
note: Tiny load.

name: Wi-Fi router / modem
note: Tiny load.

name: Security camera (plug-in)
note: Tiny load. Outdoors, keep the plug in a weatherproof box.

name: TV
note: Usually 50-200 W.

name: Radio / Bluetooth speaker
note: Small load.
